messages:
Lina Chen: Heads up — small experiment for next Wed's weekly triage. Proposal: split into a 10-minute 'hot lane' (P0s / quick fixes) + 20-minute 'backlog lane' (bug review, owner assignment) and add a rotating 'float' owner who owns follow-ups and handoffs during the week. Draft agenda:
- hot lane (10m)
- backlog lane (20m)
- quick handoffs & follow-ups (5m)
Total ~35m. Trial for 2 weeks and see if it reduces post-triage churn. Thoughts?

Sam Ortiz: +1 on the float idea. Could we also use a clear reaction to mark claimed bugs (e.g. :white_check_mark: ) so we don't lose ownership in the thread?

Tony Park: I can take the float for the week of 2026-04-05. Also propose a tiny automation: a slack shortcut `/triage-claim <issue>` that adds the owner and the :white_check_mark: reaction.

Maria Gomez: Agree with float. One ask — 35m might be heavy on backlog-heavy weeks. Can we try a 30m variant (10m hot + 15m backlog + 5m handoffs) and alternate weeks? Also let's keep a short async notes doc so people can add items ahead of time.

Alex R.: +1 to alternating lengths. Also add a 2-minute 'blocked PRs' lightning slot inside the hot lane so reviewers get a heads-up.

Lina Chen: Good call. Plan: alternate 35m/30m weeks, add a shared doc for async pre-reads, and introduce the float rotation. I'll update the calendar invite and add an agenda template. Sam — can you take the automation task for `/triage-claim`? Example usage: ` /triage-claim RED-452 @Sam` (adds owner, comment, reacts).

Sam Ortiz: Yep i'll file a small GH issue for the shortcut and wire up a simple bot reaction. Will add `:triage:` emoji to the invite so people know to react.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next triage scheduled Wed 2026-04-07 10:00am PT — calendar invite updated with 'hot/backlog/float' agenda.

Tony Park: :thumbsup: I'm set for week of 4/5 and will drop handoff notes into the doc after the meeting.
